# Research and Draft Short Social Media Captions with Perplexity

**Hook:** By the end of this guide, you can turn a fuzzy idea into a ready-to-post social media caption backed by real sources — whether you manage a personal account or post on behalf of a small business. This is for beginners who want to save time without sounding robotic.

## Before you start

- **A free Perplexity account** — sign up at the Perplexity homepage with an email or social login. A free plan is enough for this guide; Perplexity Pro (paid) gives more daily searches and access to advanced AI models.
- **A device with a browser** — Perplexity works on desktop, mobile web, and the iOS/Android apps. Screens look similar across all three.
- **A topic in mind** — even something rough, like "sustainable coffee" or "weekend hiking near Brisbane".
- **Rough total time: 15–20 minutes.**

> **One honest note:** Perplexity can research facts, summarise articles, and draft captions, but it can't post to social media for you — you'll still copy the caption into Instagram, LinkedIn, X, or your scheduler.

## Step 1 — Open Perplexity and start a new thread

Open Perplexity in your browser or app, then sign in if prompted. Look for a **"New Thread"** button or a clean search box at the top of the screen — it usually has placeholder text like *"Ask anything…"* or *"What do you want to know?"*. Click or tap inside the box. The cursor blinks, ready for typing.

If your screen looks different, look for a **pencil icon**, a **"+" button**, or a **"Home"** tab that returns you to a blank search box. Each Perplexity conversation is called a "thread", so starting fresh keeps your research tidy.

**You'll know it worked when** the page reloads with an empty box and no previous answers above it.

## Step 2 — Ask Perplexity to research trending angles for your topic

Type a clear, specific question into the search box. Beating your hands at the keyboard here won't help — give Perplexity a **topic**, an **audience**, and a **goal** in plain English. After you press Enter (or tap the arrow icon), Perplexity starts writing a short answer with **numbered footnotes** — those tiny superscript numbers are links to the sources it used. Below the answer, you'll often see a list of **related questions** you can click for a deeper dig.

If the answer feels too generic, try the **"Focus"** dropdown (look for buttons labelled **Web**, **Social**, **Academic**, or **All**) — switching to **Social** tells Perplexity to lean on posts and trending discussions rather than formal articles.

💬 Example: *"I'm writing a 3-sentence Instagram caption for a small Aussie coffee roastery. What are 5 trending topics in sustainable coffee right now in Australia, with sources from 2025 or 2026?"*

**You'll know it worked when** Perplexity returns an answer with at least 3 numbered footnote links you can tap to read the underlying articles.

## Step 3 — Pick one angle and ask for supporting facts

Scroll through the answer and choose **one** angle that excites you — don't try to cover all five. Click the related question that matches your pick, or type a new follow-up question into the same box. A new answer appears below the first, still with its own numbered sources. The conversation history stays visible, so you can scroll up and compare.

If a footnote link looks interesting, click it — Perplexity opens the source in a new tab. Don't worry about reading every word; skim for a quote, a stat, or a phrase you might want to mention.

💬 Example: *"Tell me more about the rise of compostable coffee pods in Australia. Give me 3 specific statistics or quotes from Australian sources I could mention in a post."*

**You'll know it worked when** you have one sentence or stat from a source you'd be happy to credit in your caption.

## Step 4 — Switch into "drafting mode" with a clear instruction

Now you've done the research — time to write. Stay in the same Perplexity thread and type a new prompt. This time, you're telling Perplexity to **write**, not research. Be specific about the **platform**, **length**, **tone**, and what facts to include. Perplexity drafts a caption right inside the chat.

If the tone feels off, try adding words like "warm", "playful", "matter-of-fact", or "professional" to your instruction. Perplexity works best when you tell it exactly how the caption should sound.

💬 Example: *"Write a 3-sentence Instagram caption for our compostable coffee pods. Tone: warm and friendly, not salesy. Mention that 1 in 3 Aussies now look for compostable packaging, according to a 2025 survey. End with a question to invite comments."*

**You'll know it worked when** Perplexity produces a short caption (3 sentences or so) that includes your chosen fact and ends with a question or call-to-action.

## Step 5 — Refine the draft in the same conversation

Read the caption out loud — does it sound like you? If a sentence feels clunky, type a quick refinement request right below the draft. Perplexity updates the answer in place, and the old version scrolls up so you can compare. This back-and-forth is normal and usually takes 2–3 quick rounds.

If Perplexity suggests adding emojis and you'd rather skip them, just say so. The same goes for hashtags — you can ask it to suggest 3–5 relevant ones or to leave them out entirely.

💬 Example: *"Make sentence 2 shorter and a bit punchier. Keep the question at the end. Suggest 5 relevant hashtags."*

**You'll know it worked when** the caption sounds natural when you read it aloud, includes your key fact, and fits the platform's vibe.

## Step 6 — Save your sources and copy the caption

Before you leave Perplexity, capture the **footnote links** from Steps 2 and 3 — you may want to credit a source in your post, or come back to read more later. Look for the small numbered superscripts next to sentences; click them to copy the URL from your browser's address bar.

Then copy the caption itself. Look for a small **copy icon** (two overlapping squares) near the draft, or simply highlight the text with your mouse or finger and copy it. Paste it straight into Instagram, LinkedIn, X, or your scheduling tool.

If Perplexity's Pro plan would help you here, note that the **free plan has a daily cap on Pro searches**, but regular searches are unlimited for most users — you can complete this whole guide on the free tier.

**You'll know it worked when** you have the final caption ready to paste, plus 2–3 source links saved in case you want to reference them later.

## Common mistakes

- **Mistake:** Asking one giant question like *"Write me a caption about coffee."* **Fix:** Always include the **topic**, the **audience**, the **platform**, and the **length** — specificity saves you a round-trip.
- **Mistake:** Trusting Perplexity's footnotes without checking one or two. **Fix:** Click at least one source to confirm the stat or quote actually says what Perplexity implied. AI can misread a source.
- **Mistake:** Forgetting to add a human touch. **Fix:** After copying the caption, change one small thing — a word, an emoji, your own opener — so it sounds like *you*, not a template.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** Posting about a hobby, a trip, or a family milestone becomes a 10-minute task instead of a 30-minute staring-at-the-screen session.
- **For your business or work:** You can keep a steady posting rhythm without paying an agency, and every caption can be backed by a real source — handy if you ever get asked "where did you get that number?"
- **If you're just getting started:** Treat the first caption as practice, not a masterpiece. The second one will already feel easier.

## Try it now

Open Perplexity, type this exact prompt, and watch what comes back:

> *"I'm writing a 2-sentence LinkedIn post for a small accounting firm in Melbourne. Find 1 recent statistic about AI tools being used by Australian small businesses in 2025 or 2026, with a source. Then draft the post in a confident but friendly tone, ending with a question."*

You should have a researched, source-backed draft within 2 minutes.
